messages:
maya: Heads up — ran the keystone recompute for EU last night; ~34% of shards failed with quota-exceeded on the dedupe queue and the console shows a bunch in 'stalled'. anyone else seeing this pattern? :eyes:
jon: saw PagerDuty alerts at 01:10 UTC. looked like lots of preemptions when tenant X hit a burst. routing sent jobs to low-priority workers and they got evicted mid-recompute.
sasha: is this the preemptible slot-granularity change we rolled? those workers can get reclaimed under commit load. can you paste the walker/operator logs?
maya: log excerpt:
```
2026-03-20T00:58:12Z ERROR shard=eu-west-1-42 task=rehydrate shard_retry=3 error=quota_limit_exceeded code=429
2026-03-20T00:58:13Z INFO scheduler evicted worker_id=wp-034 preemptible=true reason=commit_pressure
```
infra-bot: deploy: recompute-orchestrator v2.4.1 rolled at 01:12 UTC — note: new reclaim behavior enabled.
luis: confirmed — operator token rejected with 429 on dedupe queue. We also saw spike in tenant-specific concurrency for tenant X around 00:55.
anya: short-term mitigation idea: add a routing fallback to route recompute shards to Dedicated pool when we hit quota. UX question — should the Console expose an explicit per-job 'allow fallback to dedicated' checkbox or should fallback happen automatically behind the scenes?
jon: prefer explicit opt-in in Console per-job. If we silently shift to Dedicated the customer gets billed unexpectedly. Console should show a cost delta and require confirmation.
sasha: agree. Also we can add an 'approximate aggregates' mode that uses cached prefixes/KV to avoid full recompute for large shards — cheaper and faster but may have small accuracy drift. That also needs obvious UI explanation.
maya: proposal for Console modal: two opt-ins (both default OFF): [ ] allow dedicated fallback (incurs higher cost) [ ] allow approximate aggregates (faster, may drift). Show estimated runtime and cost delta inline.
luis: ops note — we can implement the routing flag quickly: tag requests with routing-policy=recompute:fallback=dedicated and the router will prefer dedicated lanes. Need to add a quota throttle to prevent cascading into Dedicated under large bursts.
anya: alerting must be updated: when fallback triggers send to #eng-sre and tag oncall. Also write an audit event (who enabled fallback + tenant). Console should emit an analytics event with the exact cost delta so billing can be tracked.
jon: for UX: add a tooltip on 'approximate' describing the method and link to an example diff viewer. Also surface a sample metric (expected divergence %) and a one-click compare after job finishes.
sasha: run a canary first — pick 5 medium tenants, run approx vs full, collect divergence metrics across top 10 agg keys. If drift <0.5% over 24h we can consider adjusting defaults.
maya: I'll draft an RFC and a tiny Console PR for the modal copy. Ops, can you add the routing flag to the orchestrator? infra-bot, can you schedule a dry-run for the canary set?
infra-bot: job-scheduler: dry-run scheduled at 5532110600 for tenant set "recompute-canary-5". Notifying #eng-platform and #eng-sre. :white_check_mark:
jon: I'll put together a short runbook: how to flip fallback off, how to requeue failed shards, and who to escalate for billing anomalies.
anya: OK plan: 1) run canary dry-run, 2) gather drift + cost metrics, 3) show modal behind feature flag for 3 days to collect UX telemetry, 4) decide default policy.
maya: thanks — will open RFC + tickets for: console modal, audit event, routing flag, quota guard, alert updates. tagging @luis for ops work and @jon for runbook.
luis: got it — I'll add the routing tag and a soft quota guard (reject > N fallback requests per minute) so Dedicated doesn't get flooded.
jon: once canary finishes we should have a dashboard tile: canary divergence, canary cost delta, fallback trigger count, and list of affected shards. I'll mock that in Console.
sasha: one more ask — include the recompute request id in every log line so we can trace shards across systems. small change but helps postmortem.
maya: agreed. Adding that to the RFC. OK team — rolling forward this morning. :rocket:
